item.title: Fifth Post
item.description:
Reflection on Inclusive terminology Presentation

Out of all presentations, the presentation on inclusive terminology caught my eye. I never had thought about it that way because for instance when you hear blacklist, the only thing I can make out of the word is litreally blacklist, or someone or something getting blacklisted. However, I still feel it’s kind dumb because I feel this example particularly is inculcating the belief of black as in blacklist being racist which never once striked my mind. I have only ever associated it with someone or smothing being banned or blocked. Well, as the presentation continued, I got to know that inclusive terminolgy is not just whether a person personally finds them offfensive; it’s about how words/language might shape society and perception beyond meaning or emotion. Even though most people do not associate the term blacklist with negative ideas, the argument is that it is repeated association of black with negative meaning and white with postive meaning can reinforce the certain bias in the society. I appreciated the critical thinking in the presentaion about somthing I never really thought about and how language evovles overtime with society. It kinds of matches with the motto of our university as well:)

item.title: fourth Post
item.description:
Reflection on Projects

So, with the projects I feel I did learn significantly, especially metabase where i struggled a lot creating somthing meaningful and unique. In metabase, I tried to count the number of stations which collect data regarding these different kinds of pollutant; however I forgot that set of data was a recording collected by the station. I could have probably solved this by summarize query which would have grouped the duplicated into a singular entitiy. Making the chatbot was really fun honestly. My idea to not make a typical chat, make the whole expirience as if someone is going through a game before buying it. Well, the idea was far to ambitious, but still i ended up with somethin quite unique as well. Creating the initial page was the most difficult part of all. The custom CSS and understanding the typebot’s class selectors was really hectic. I mostly used the typebot’s documentation, stack overflow, DevTools for troubleshooting. Well, made me realize that learning new things require time and effort, and most of all patience.

item.title: Third Post
item.description:
Failure Wiki

Reading about the post office scandal which happened in the UK due to technical glitches caused by software called ‘Horizon’, developed by the Japanese company Fujitsu, led to one of the most devastating institutional failures.

This scandal made me realise how comfort or ignorance of something can lead to disastrous outcomes. Unfortunately, over a thousand sub-postmasters were wrongfully prosecuted and some even comitted the suicide. People placing their comfort in the assumption that technology is always accurate is vastly the reason why these events happened in the first place.

item.title: Second Post
item.description:
Optimization

Optimization models are genuinely so cool. While solving problems and thinking this must be the answers now, you figure that you were so wrong.

Well, I did not except it to be straightforward either. I quickly understood that there’s much more about how you think rather than what you know. Almost all the time, my instinct led me in the wrong direction because I overllooked things and structure of the problem.

item.title: First Post
item.description:
Github&Hugo

I think the setting up the whole reflection blog website was fun. It was moderately challenging and I feel having a reflection blog where you update about life is so introspective and also gives you with something to look upon later.

Also, I had to help my groupmates quite a lot. I think this is because they have never troubleshooted before and tried reading documentation to figure out solutions.However, they got it when I pinpointed the issue. Most of them either didn’t update their baseURL or mention the theme specifically in hugo.toml file. What I found interesting was showing them how to approach the problem rather than just giving solution. By guiding them to read through the documentation and find relevant content for deploying the site, then they were atleast able to put their head to it and make progress.
